requirement_text: UNIGE requires foreign secondary diplomas to demonstrate 'formation générale' (general education), assessed per Section 9.1 of the official conditions document against the Council of Europe/UNESCO Lisbon Convention (no. 165) and the work of swissuniversities' Commission d'admission et d'équivalences (formerly CRUS) -- confirming this is not a UNIGE-independent standard but tied directly to the same central body as the swissuniversities system file. Six subject areas required: (1) first language, (2) second language, (3) mathematics, (4) natural sciences (biology, chemistry, or physics), (5) social sciences/humanities (geography, history, or economics/law), and (6) a free-choice subject from categories 2, 4, or 5, or informatics, or philosophy.
source_authority_note: unige.ch is University of Geneva's official domain; not .edu/.ac./.gov.

requirement_text: International Baccalaureate recognition (confirmed verbatim against the authoritative PDF, Section 9.1): must have been followed continuously for the final two years; three Higher Level exams including one science (mathematics, chemistry, biology, or physics) plus three Standard Level exams from a defined subject list (all languages except theatre literature/performance, economics and business administration, business administration, geography, history, philosophy, biology, chemistry, physics, informatics, mathematics analysis/applications at either level); minimum 32 points excluding bonus points. A related but distinct pathway exists for the European Baccalaureate (Baccalauréat européen), requiring continuous enrollment for the final THREE years instead of two -- not previously captured, noted here for completeness.

requirement_text: UNIGE does NOT apply a numerus clausus or the EMS test at first-year entry to the Bachelor in Human Medicine. Progression from 1st to 2nd year instead happens via a competitive exam ('concours'), introduced starting 2017-2018: 'Dès 2017-2018, conformément à l'article 17 (5) de la Loi sur l'Université, le Rectorat a autorisé l'instauration d'un concours pour le passage de la 1ère à la 2ème année' (as of 2017-2018, per Article 17(5) of the University Law, the Rectorate authorized a competitive exam for progression from 1st to 2nd year). First-year assessment comprises three partial evaluations (ESMS, ESFO, ESMB); passing requires a score ≥4.0, but passing alone does not guarantee 2nd-year admission — ranking against available capacity decides. Students scoring 3.0–3.75, or who pass without being admitted, may retake the exam once.

limitations: This page focuses on the 1st-year exam structure and 2nd-year progression; it does not itself state UNIGE's foreign-qualification requirements for FIRST-year entry to medicine (those follow UNIGE's general bachelor admission rules recorded above in this file — no medicine-specific foreign-qualification variant was found).
